case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: In a foster-care class action the court recognized that foster children hold a substantive due process right to be free from unreasonable risk of harm and to reasonable safety, but held the jury was misinstructed by treating the professional-judgment standard of care as the right itself, and it narrowed the systemwide injunction.
key_cases.relevance: The class included youth who had aged out of care, and the court addressed their continuing stake in the systemic remedy.
key_cases.quote: We hold that foster children have a constitutional substantive due process right to be free from unreasonable risks of harm and a right to reasonable safety.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the discretionary right to counsel for children in RCW 13.34.100(7)(a) satisfies article I, section 3, and further held that the confidentiality of juvenile dependency records under RCW 13.50.100(2) survives appeal so appellate courts should seal such records on their own motion.
key_cases.relevance: Governs appointment of counsel for older dependent youth whose own interests in placement and transition planning may diverge from the agency's.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the confidential nature of dependency proceedings granted by RCW 13.50.100(2) is not lost through appeal

key_cases.holding: The court held that children in dependency and termination proceedings have liberty interests at least as weighty as their parents' and may constitutionally be entitled to appointed counsel, but that RCW 13.34.100(6) is constitutionally adequate because the right is not universal and is committed case by case to the trial judge's discretion.
key_cases.relevance: Recognizes the child's own liberty interest in placement and family relationships, which matters most as a youth approaches majority.
key_cases.quote: We hold the due process right of children who are subjects of dependency or termination proceedings to counsel is not universal.
